stories.title: Hormone therapy shows promise in breast cancer trial
stories.summary: A new hormone therapy reduced the risk of invasive breast cancer recurrence or death in early-stage patients compared to standard treatments. Findings from a large international phase 3 trial, co-led by UCLA Health Jonsson Comprehensive Cancer Center, suggest a potential shift in managing hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s drug targets tau protein
stories.summary: An experimental Alzheimer’s drug that reduces the production of the tau protein slowed the decline in memory and thinking skills by up to 54 percent in a clinical trial. The drug aims to address a key protein associated with the progression of the disease.

stories.title: Rare sugar d-sorbose may help control allergic and autoimmune diseases
stories.summary: Rare sugars are naturally occurring monosaccharides that are scarce in nature and are not readily used by the body as energy sources. Some have physiological effects beyond sweetness, raising interest in their potential health applications. One such sugar, d-sorbose, is a structural relative of d-fructose, but its effects on immune

stories.title: Imaging technique tracks type 1 diabetes progression
stories.summary: A molecular imaging approach measuring beta-cell mass in the pancreas offers new insights into type 1 diabetes. Research published in the Journal of Nuclear Medicine found that patients with the disease for under seven years retain higher beta-cell function and lower intrapancreatic fat than those with longer durations.

stories.title: Lab-grown brain model tests neural implants
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a laboratory cell model that mimics how the brain reacts to implanted devices. The team claims the model offers a faster, lower-cost, and more ethical alternative to existing methods for testing the safety and longevity of neural implants.

stories.title: Structural details aid search for new drugs for heart failure and pulmonary fibrosis
stories.summary: As its name suggests, a hormone called relaxin-2 is involved in relaxing tissues throughout the body, such as dilating blood vessels to increase blood flow, loosening pelvic ligaments and suppressing uterine contractions in preparation for childbirth, and reducing inflammation and scar-tissue buildup (fibrosis) in the heart, lungs, liver, kidneys and

stories.title: Sibeprenlimab maintains kidney function in IgA nephropathy
stories.summary: Patients receiving sibeprenlimab maintained nearly stable kidney function over two years, according to findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine. In contrast, kidney function declined significantly among patients in the study who received a placebo.

stories.title: Lung complications affect 1 in 3 patients receiving antibody-drug conjugates for lung cancer, study finds - Medical Xpre
Single HPV vaccine dose found effective
stories.summary: A single dose of the HPV vaccine provides protection comparable to two doses against the types responsible for most cervical cancers, according to a large randomized trial. The study of 20,330 girls showed 97 percent effectiveness with no evidence of protection declining over five years.

stories.title: ICMR’s survey finds lower anaemia prevalence across age groups compared to previous surveys - News On AIR
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research ( ICMR ) has released key findings from the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025, providing comprehensive national evidence on anaemia and micronutrient deficiencies across the life course. ICMR said, the SAMPADA findings shows an encouraging

stories.title: Time to tip scales against tuberculosis in India
stories.summary: One of the biggest challenges in front of public health policy-makers in India is that the tuberculosis bacterium is becoming increasingly resistant to the frontline anti-TB drug, isoniazid. This is the time to take ahead a strategy that researchers at Bengaluru’s Indian Institute of Science have identified to restore the

stories.title: Indiaâs Landmark Nutrition Survey Maps Shifting Anaemia Burden Across Generations
stories.summary: A sweeping nationwide health investigation conducted by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has found that the overall prevalence of anaemia across India is lower than earlier national estimates, with severe forms of the blood disorder accounting for less than two per cent of cases across most age demographics.

stories.title: “Where is accountability?”: Mallikarjun Kharge questions Centre over anaemia, malnutrition figures in ICMR-SAMPADA repor
stories.summary: New Delhi [India], November 25 (ANI): Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Wednesday questioned the Centre's accountability over the prevalence of anaemia and malnutrition among women and children, citing findings from the Indian Council of Medical Research's (ICMR) SAMPADA survey and expenditure figures under various nutrition schemes. stories.summary: Medical Updates Over 50% Indian Women Anaemic: Key ICMR SAMPADA Insights Recent findings from the ICMR-NIN SAMPADA survey highlight persistent concerns regarding anaemia prevalence in India. More than half of women in their reproductive years remain anaemic, despite long-standing national supplementation initiatives. Furthermore, the survey demonstrates an extensive burden of

stories.title: ICMR survey records lower anaemia prevalence across India - Express Healthcare
stories.summary: Severe anaemia below 2 per cent across most age groups, with the majority of cases being mild The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has released key findings from the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet

stories.title: ICMR survey finds widespread vitamin B12 deficiency
stories.summary: A national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research found that 66 percent of teenagers and 60 percent of adult men in India are deficient in vitamin B12. The study classified levels below 203 pg/mL as deficient, noting that B12 deficiency is now more common than iron deficiency.

stories.title: Anaemia incidence lower, finds ICMR survey, but over half of India's women still affected
stories.summary: New Delhi: The burden of anaemia in India is lower than that reported in previous national surveys, with severe cases accounting for less than 2 percent of most population groups, a new survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN) has found. stories.title: SAMPADA data claims lower anaemia prevalence in India than previous surveys
stories.summary: India stopped collecting anaemia data as part of NFHS, after the 5th round. This is the first time anaemia data is being published, after the measure was withdrawn from the NFHS on the grounds that the government intended to conduct a gold-standard test of drawing venous blood, instead of the

stories.title: Health Ministry : enemy targeting of Health Sector exacerbates Humanitarian situation in Yemen - وكالة سبأ
Health Ministry urges flu vigilance
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Wellness is encouraging Jamaicans to get vaccinated as cooler months approach. Chief Medical Officer Dr. Jacquiline Bisasor-McKenzie noted that influenza can lead to severe complications, particularly for children and the elderly. The ministry advises the public to treat the seasonal illness with caution.

stories.title: Highway fire in Egypt kills 30
stories.summary: A fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo has resulted in at least 30 deaths, according to Egypt’s Health Ministry. The incident occurred on a primary transit route. Further details regarding the cause of the fire have not been released.

stories.title: WHO monitors new COVID-19 variant
stories.summary: The WHO has designated the PJ.2.1 COVID-19 lineage as a variant under monitoring. While detection frequency is trending upward globally, clinical findings provide no clear confirmation that the strain is more transmissible or causes more acute health complications than previous versions of the virus.

stories.title: COVID-19 cases rise as experts advise vaccination
stories.summary: COVID-19 cases are increasing alongside an early start to the influenza season. Experts continue to recommend updated vaccinations to reduce the risk of severe disease and transmission. Respiratory viruses are currently contributing to school and work absences, according to Canadian surveillance reports.

stories.title: WHO chief calls for end to fuel blockade on Cuba
stories.summary: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has called for the immediate lifting of U.S. fuel restrictions on Cuba, citing risks to children and vulnerable populations. The organization pledged $2 million to support the nation's immunization program during the official's visit to Havana healthcare facilities.

stories.title: California measles cases hit 60 for 2026
stories.summary: California has recorded 60 measles cases this year, four times the 2024 total. Every case involved an unvaccinated individual or one with unknown status. The state's count follows the Pan American Health Organization ending the United States' measles elimination status, which had been held since 2000.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry declares meningitis alert
stories.summary: The Palestinian Ministry of Health in Gaza has declared an epidemic alert following 15 deaths and a surge in meningitis cases. Infections reached 272 in October, more than eight times the usual monthly average, as deteriorating infrastructure continues to impact local sanitation and water access.

stories.title: Japan holds first Ebola response drill
stories.summary: Japan conducted a crisis management drill simulating a domestic Ebola case in Fukuoka. The exercise involved the Prime Minister and health officials, following the WHO's international emergency declaration regarding the outbreak in Congo. The government has held annual infectious disease response drills since 2023.

stories.title: AI model identifies psoriasis from photos
stories.summary: A study published in Frontiers in Medicine suggests ChatGPT-5 can identify psoriasis and assess its severity from a single photo with nearly 100 percent accuracy. Researchers at Semmelweis University noted the results are promising, though they cautioned that artificial intelligence is not a substitute for clinical diagnosis.

stories.title: Q&A: Jonathan Bush on the evolution of digital health and the future of EHRs - MobiHealthNews
India projects need for 1.25 million digital health workers
stories.summary: A FICCI-KPMG report projects India will need to train 1.25 million healthcare professionals annually in digital health and AI through 2035. The platform Benevolve is now offering skills intelligence tools to help employers manage this transition as the country prepares for 20 new AI-enabled healthcare roles.

stories.title: AIIMS Delhi expands voice prescription tool
stories.summary: The All India Institute of Medical Sciences has expanded its use of the BHASHINI voice prescription tool following a pilot in its neurology departments. The technology allows doctors to dictate prescriptions directly into hospital systems, aiming to reduce manual documentation loads for healthcare staff.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission emerges as one of world’s largest digital health ecosystems with over 93.95 crore ABHA I
AIIMS Delhi rolls out voice-to-text prescriptions
stories.summary: AIIMS Delhi is deploying the BHASHINI voice prescription tool to link speech-to-text technology with the eHospital module. The government-backed platform aims to cut documentation time for doctors during outpatient consultations. The rollout is part of a broader effort to manage administrative burdens in public healthcare settings.

stories.title: Research examines mRNA vaccine and tumor signaling
stories.summary: A perspective in Oncotarget explores theoretical biological mechanisms by which mRNA vaccines and Spike proteins might influence tumor cell signaling. The author acknowledges that there is currently no formal evidence of an association between COVID-19 vaccines and the development of tumors.

stories.title: Jim Mackey to step down as NHS England chief executive - Home | Digital Health
Who oversees digital health? Providers face a regulatory maze - Healthcare Dive
Youth are turning to AI for mental health support
stories.summary: AI is increasingly being used to manage mental health, according to recent reports. The technology is being applied to areas of life previously reserved for human interaction. It is a shift in how individuals approach their personal well-being.

stories.title: Exercise interventions show modest mental health benefits for children
stories.summary: A systematic review of physical activity and sport interventions for children in China found evidence favoring some mental health outcomes. Comparative evidence for physical health remains limited and inconclusive. The research analyzed studies published up to 5 August 2026 across nine databases.

stories.title: Study identifies why school mental health programs falter
stories.summary: Research led by Kristel Jenniskens reveals that while school-based anxiety and depression interventions often succeed in clinical trials, few achieve widespread implementation. The study examined 181 trials to determine why evidence-based programs frequently fail after experimental funding concludes. Funding is a known variable in sustainability.

stories.title: Body awareness linked to body satisfaction in teenage girls
stories.summary: Teenage girls who are better at recognizing internal bodily signals tend to be happier with their appearance, according to new research. The study suggests a connection between interoceptive awareness and self-perception during adolescence.

stories.title: Mindfulness linked to better mental health and social media habits
stories.summary: A review published 25 November 2026 in PLOS One by researchers at University College London associates mindfulness with improved mental health and more beneficial patterns of social media use. The study highlights a correlation between present-moment awareness and digital behavior.

stories.title: Students are using AI as a mental health counselor
stories.summary: A survey of 2,020 students at the University of Bath, published in JMIR Mental Health, found that one in four respondents used generative AI for mental health support in the past six months. The study had a 9.1 percent response rate.

stories.title: One in four students use AI for mental health support
stories.summary: A peer-reviewed study from the University of Bath found that one in four surveyed students used AI for mental health support in the past six months. Use was highest among students reporting very low well-being. The software is being treated as a personal therapist.

stories.title: One in four students turn to AI for mental health support - Social Care Today
Short form social media videos linked to teen mental health crisis
stories.summary: Dr. Victor Fornari, a child and adolescent psychiatrist at Northwell Health, discussed the link between short form social media videos and the current teen mental health crisis. The conversation addressed the potential impact of rapid-fire digital content on adolescent well-being.

research.title: Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains
research.summary: Nearly one in three older adults with dementia or other cognitive disorders takes potentially harmful medications that can worsen brain function and increase the risk of hospitalization and premature death. Despite encouraging progress over the past decade, researchers warn that medication-related harm remains a major and potentially preventable.

research.title: STEP Young trial shows semaglutide benefits in children
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 25 November 2026, doi:10.1038/d41591-026-00059-7 In a phase 3 study, children with obesity lost significantly more weight with semaglutide than with placebo, with more than one third achieving a body mass index below the threshold for obesity.

research.title: Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer
research.summary: A common antibody in the gut may be a powerful natural defense against colon cancer, with researchers finding that mice lacking it developed more than twice as many tumors. Restoring the antibody eliminated the increased risk, revealing a promising new avenue for preventing cancer before it starts.

research.title: Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety
research.summary: An AI-powered analysis of thousands of children's brain scans has revealed three distinct brain types underlying ADHD and anxiety that do not neatly fit traditional diagnoses. These hidden biological patterns can appear before a diagnosis is made, potentially enabling earlier detection and more effective, personalized treatments.

research.title: How waistlines, organ function tell a better story of obesity than BMI does
research.summary: In 2025, The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology established a commission of 58 experts from different countries to set obesity-related guidelines. A new study in Nature has tested whether the commission’s recommendations can actually distinguish between people at different levels of risk, with data from 8.4 lakh adults
